original_question: Let e be an edge of a graph G. Is the list packing number of G always at most two more than the list packing number of the edge-deleted graph G \ e? Equivalently, must chi*_l(G) <= chi*_l(G \ e) + 2 hold for every graph G and every edge e of G?
target_in_paper: Section 2, "Various open problems related to list packing," subsection "Removing an edge or vertex," Problem 2.9, second question (the edge-deletion version).
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right target very closely: it uses the correct invariant (the list packing number, denoted χ^*_ℓ), the correct graph operation (deleting a single edge), the correct additive constant (+2), and the correct universal scope (for every graph G and every edge e of G). It also correctly turns the verbal question into the symbolic inequality χ^*_ℓ(G) <= χ^*_ℓ(G \ e) + 2.
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, it should define χ^*_ℓ(H): the least integer k such that every k-list-assignment L on H admits an L-packing of size k, i.e. k pairwise disjoint proper L-colourings.
It should explicitly specify that e is an edge of G (e ∈ E(G)) and that G \ e denotes the graph obtained from G by deleting e.
The paper states this as the second half of a paired deletion problem (the first half is the analogous vertex-deletion question); that relation is implicit in your draft.
The ambient graph-theoretic setting is left implicit in the draft, just as in the paper's surrounding section.
refined_question: Let G be a graph and let e ∈ E(G). Write G \ e for the graph obtained by deleting e. If χ^*_ℓ(H) denotes the list packing number of a graph H, meaning the least integer k such that every k-list-assignment on H admits k pairwise disjoint proper list-colourings, must one always have χ^*_ℓ(G) <= χ^*_ℓ(G \ e) + 2?
justification: The exact paper-faithful target is not a conjecture or theorem label, but the second question in Problem 2.9 of Section 2. The surrounding text first defines list assignments, disjoint L-colourings, L-packings, and the list packing number χ^*_ℓ(G), and then asks, in the subsection "Removing an edge or vertex," whether deleting a vertex or deleting an edge can increase χ^*_ℓ by more than 2. Your draft isolates precisely the edge-deletion half of that problem and does not broaden it beyond the paper. The only substantive additions needed are the local definitions that make the question stand alone.
